scope: Hash-identical isolated crate scan, not final production graph
re_review: Re-review 2026-11-03 (Windows ARM64 source support, CEO decision 2026-11-03): src/lib.rs widened the compile-time gate from x86_64 to the explicit allow-list {x86_64, aarch64} with MSVC and compiles platform.rs for both; build.rs keeps host equal to target and additionally requires the rustc host line to equal the target (OSN-22); src/platform.rs reads the COFF Machine field (NT headers + 4) inside the existing image() unsafe block, beside the already-read signature, magic and image size of the same loader-validated headers, and fails closed through the existing boundary_failure() when it is not 0x8664 on x86_64 (0xAA64 on aarch64); its SAFETY comments now name the target's system ABI and the PE32+ TLS directory instead of x64 only. No unsafe block, unsafe function, unsafe impl, foreign declaration, exported symbol, link section or ABI layout was added or changed. For x86_64 the unsafe semantics are unchanged: a loader-mapped x64 image always carries Machine 0x8664, so the extra in-bounds read cannot change an accepted image's path, and every refusal is the pre-existing fail-closed exit. Re-measured on native x64 Windows with cargo-geiger 0.14.0 by the original isolated-package method (byte-identical src/lib.rs, src/platform.rs and build.rs; scratch manifest with a local lint declaration); the same method reproduced the previous 2/45/1 counts for the previous sources. Used unsafe exposure is 2 functions, 48 expressions (was 45: the one added Machine read) and 1 implementation, with zero unused unsafe. The scratch Geiger report was not retained in the repository, as before; only its digest is recorded. The aarch64 build of this file is reviewed here but not executed or qualified: this x64 host cannot run ARM64 code, and ARM64 evidence must come from a native ARM64 host.
